ip_top_stories.title: First AI Copyright Appeal's Reach Hinges on Market Impact Issue
ip_top_stories.summary: The first AI copyright appeal is being closely watched as courts consider how broadly its ruling may apply, with the key question centring on market impact — specifically whether AI-generated or AI-trained outputs harm the market for original works. The outcome could set a significant precedent for fair use analysis in AI copyright cases.

ip_top_stories.title: Anthropic, Nvidia Sway Judge to Split Authors' AI Copyright Suit
ip_top_stories.summary: A judge has agreed to split an authors' AI copyright lawsuit following arguments from Anthropic and Nvidia, requiring authors to pursue their claims separately. The ruling has procedural implications for how AI copyright cases are structured and litigated going forward.

ip_top_stories.title: Google Moves to Dismiss Artists' AI Lawsuit, Citing YouTube Terms
ip_top_stories.summary: Google has filed a motion to dismiss a lawsuit brought by independent artists over its Lyria 3 AI music model, arguing that artists consented to their music being used for AI training when they agreed to YouTube's terms of service. The case raises significant questions about whether platform terms of service can constitute licensing consent for AI training purposes.

ip_top_stories.title: The CNN-Perplexity Lawsuit Is Not Just Another AI Copyright Case
ip_top_stories.summary: Analysis of CNN's lawsuit against Perplexity AI argues the case goes beyond standard AI copyright disputes, potentially addressing questions of brand liability and AI visibility risks for publishers. The piece examines what makes this case legally distinct and its broader implications for news organisations.

ip_top_stories.title: Who's suing AI and who's signing: Brazil's Folha settles OpenAI lawsuit with commercial deal
ip_top_stories.summary: Brazilian newspaper Folha de S.Paulo has settled its copyright lawsuit against OpenAI by entering into a commercial licensing deal, highlighting the diverging strategies publishers are taking — litigation versus licensing — in response to AI training on their content.

ip_further_links.title: Authors must pursue AI copyright claims separately, judge rules
ip_further_links.summary: A judge has ruled that authors cannot bring consolidated AI copyright claims and must instead pursue their cases individually, a decision that could raise the cost and complexity of litigation for creators.

ip_further_links.title: Meta AI Order Offers Novel Question For 9th Circ., Authors Say
ip_further_links.summary: Authors argue that a Meta AI-related court order raises a novel legal question for the Ninth Circuit with potential implications for how AI copyright claims are handled at the appellate level.

ip_further_links.title: France's cultural sector groups denounce parliamentary obstruction over AI legislation
ip_further_links.summary: French cultural sector organisations have condemned what they describe as parliamentary obstruction blocking progress on AI legislation they say is needed to protect creators' rights.

ip_further_links.title: Canada's AI strategy doesn't mention copyright. Ottawa says 'stay tuned'
ip_further_links.summary: Canada's newly released AI strategy contains no reference to copyright, prompting concern from creators and publishers, with the government offering only a vague assurance that the issue will be addressed.

ip_further_links.title: New AI advertisement law goes into effect in New York requiring 'synthetic performer' label
ip_further_links.summary: A new New York law now requires AI-generated performers in advertisements to be labelled as 'synthetic performers', marking one of the first US state-level regulations addressing AI-generated likenesses in commercial content.

ip_further_links.title: Landmark German ruling declares Google's AI Overviews are Google's own words and makes it liable for false answers
ip_further_links.summary: A German court has ruled that Google is liable for inaccurate statements made in its AI Overviews feature, finding that the AI-generated summaries constitute Google's own speech rather than a neutral aggregation of third-party content.

ip_further_links.title: Building Scholar-Ready AI: A Conversation with Todd Toler
ip_further_links.summary: The Scholarly Kitchen interviews Todd Toler about what it means to build AI tools designed specifically for academic and research contexts, covering issues of source quality, licensing, and trust.

ip_further_links.title: Copyright law 'struggling' to parse AI's ascendancy
ip_further_links.summary: A broad analysis finds that existing copyright frameworks are under significant strain as AI systems grow more capable, with legal experts noting that courts and legislators are yet to provide clear and consistent answers.

ip_further_links.title: Wolters Kluwer expands its Libra AI workspace with authoritative Swiss legal content from leading publisher Stämpfli
ip_further_links.summary: Wolters Kluwer has announced a licensing agreement with Swiss legal publisher Stämpfli to integrate authoritative Swiss legal content into its Libra AI legal workspace platform.

ip_further_links.title: CNN sues Perplexity over AI copyright claims as brands face new risks around AI visibility
ip_further_links.summary: CNN has filed a copyright lawsuit against Perplexity AI, with the case also highlighting broader commercial risks for brands as AI systems increasingly mediate content discovery and visibility.
